path: Three background patterns that the category lacks, each a drawing idea of its own rather than a variation on one already shipped: a woven ribbon surface where strands pass over and under, an irregular triangulated mesh with drawn nodes, and diagonals built only from square stair steps. They are plain geometry and public ornament idioms, so each is originated and carries no credits, and nothing here is built from a capture, a shortlist, or anyone's component. Each is generated geometry on an under layer, with no randomness except the seeded mesh. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, every default is a pure function of its props, and every default already looks finished and quiet enough to sit under a headline on the dark ground and the light one. All design, building, and review of this wave runs through Claude CLI sessions.

components.title: Weave Lines
components.brief: A woven surface drawn as outlined ribbons. Horizontal and vertical strands lie on a square grid of `pitch` px, each strand a ribbon whose two long edges are hairlines, `ribbon` times the pitch apart, with a clear gutter of ground between neighbouring strands. At every crossing one strand passes over the other, and that is the whole idea: the over strand's two edge lines run unbroken through the crossing, while the under strand's two edge lines stop short of the over strand's edges by `gap` px and start again on the far side, so the eye reads the under strand as tucked beneath. No fill is drawn anywhere, because the ground must show through, so the occlusion is made only of those breaks. Which strand is over comes from the crossing's column i and row j: horizontal is over when floor(i / float) + floor(j / float) is even, and vertical is over otherwise. With `float` 1 each strand goes over, under, over, under, which is a plain weave. With 2 it goes over two crossings and under two, so the surface breaks into 2 by 2 blocks of horizontal ribbons and vertical ribbons, which is a basket weave, and 3 gives larger blocks. Nothing is random and nothing is rotated, so the same props always draw the same surface from the host's top left corner. Draw it as one inline SVG on an under layer from lib/host.ts, filled with a single svg pattern tile whose period is twice `float` times `pitch` on each side, so no resize observer is needed and the cost stays flat at any host size; every line is a hairline in fg through cssVar, drawn at one pixel with square caps and crisp edges, and `strength` is the layer's opacity. It is a background: pointer-events none, aria-hidden, children above, and it never hides or moves what it wraps. Nothing moves, so reduced motion needs no extra frame. Follow registry/patterns/truchet-tiles for the under layer, the inline SVG, and the lifecycle, and registry/patterns/hatch-lines for the shape of a pattern with a few numeric props. The nearest shipped sibling is hatch-lines, and the distinction is exact: hatch-lines draws two or three families of parallel lines at an angle that all cross and overlap with nothing in front of anything, so it reads as a net or an engraving, while weave-lines draws only horizontal and vertical ribbons, each with two edge lines, and breaks the under strand at every crossing, so it reads as cloth. It is also not grid-paper, which is one continuous orthogonal grid with no breaks, not checkerboard, which fills squares, and not brick-lattice, which offsets rows of rectangles. The wave 9 bohemian hero uses a woven motif as one ornament inside a page, and this is a full field with its own props and no relation to it. A capture at 1280 px shows the field across the whole frame at the 24 px default, the plain over and under rhythm clearly legible in the first few crossings of any row and column, the two edges of every ribbon visible, the gutters open, and a headline set over it readable. A capture at 390 px shows the same field at the same pitch, about sixteen strands across, cut cleanly at the frame's edge with no half-drawn artifact, and nothing scaled down to fit. It is wrong if an under strand's edge line is drawn through an over strand, because then it is a grid of crossing lines and not a weave; if two neighbouring crossings along one strand are both over or both under at `float` 1, so the alternation fails; if the breaks are so small at the default that the field reads as a plain grid at 1280 px; if the ribbons touch each other so that no gutter remains; if any line is blurred across two pixel rows instead of landing crisp; or if the default is loud enough that a headline set over it loses contrast on either ground. Set meta.wraps to "content", meta.facets to ["static", "background"], meta.palette to ["fg"], and meta.demo children to a short heading over a line of copy. No meta.host, stage, controlled, or interactions. Patterns have 6144 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 2.2 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes no random number at all, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: pitch (12 to 48 px between strand centres, default 24), float (1 to 3 crossings a strand passes over before passing under, default 1), ribbon (0.5 to 0.9, the ribbon width as a fraction of the pitch, default 0.75), gap (1 to 6 px the under strand's edges stop short of the over strand, default 3), strength (0 to 1, the layer's opacity, default 0.35). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Triangular Mesh
components.brief: An irregular triangulated mesh, the wireframe of a low poly surface: a field of nodes joined by straight hairline edges into triangles, with a small dot drawn at every node, and a few nodes marked in the accent. Build it from a jittered lattice. Nodes sit on a square lattice of `cell` px, indexed by column c and row r, and each node is displaced by a seeded offset on each axis of up to `jitter` times `cell` divided by two, drawn from createRng(hashSeed(seed, c, r)), so a node's position depends only on its own indices and the seed, and growing or shrinking the host only adds or removes nodes without moving any that remain. Lattice nodes extend one column and row beyond the host so no edge is cut short at the frame. The edges are the lattice's horizontal and vertical neighbours plus one diagonal in every quad of four nodes. For each quad, take the diagonal that keeps both resulting triangles wound the same way as the quad, so a triangle is never turned inside out, and when both diagonals qualify take the shorter one, with ties going from top left to bottom right. Every face of the result is therefore a triangle, and no edge crosses another. Each edge is drawn once, in one path, in fg through cssVar at one pixel. Each node is a filled dot of about 1.5 px radius in fg. A node is marked when createRng(hashSeed(seed, c, r, 1))() is below `marks` divided by 100, and a marked node is drawn as a larger filled dot of about 3 px radius in the accent, skipped when it lies within its radius plus 2 px of the frame's edge so no mark can read as clipped, so the accent appears in one place for one reason: it picks out a few vertices. `strength` is the opacity of the edges, nodes sit a little above it and never above one, and accent marks are drawn at a fixed high opacity so they stay findable at the whisper default; with `nodes` off the dots go and only the edges and the accent marks remain. Draw one inline SVG inside an under layer from lib/host.ts, sized to the host's pixel box and rebuilt on resize through a ResizeObserver, exactly as truchet-tiles does, and set picaReady after the first complete build. It is a background: pointer-events none, aria-hidden, children above. Nothing moves. Follow registry/patterns/truchet-tiles for the under layer, the per cell hashed seed, the rebuild on resize, and the lifecycle, and registry/patterns/circuit-traces for the accent mark. The nearest siblings are cell-mosaic and isometric-grid, and the distinctions are exact. Cell-mosaic is a Voronoi field: its cells are polygons of four to seven sides, it draws no nodes, and it has no row or column order. Triangular-mesh has only triangles, draws every node as a dot, and keeps a legible lattice of rows and columns under the jitter, so it reads as a wireframe and not as cells. Isometric-grid is perfectly regular, three straight axes of equilateral triangles with no variation, and the minimum jitter here is 0.1 so this never collapses into a regular grid or a right triangle grid. It is also not truchet-tiles, which has no triangles and no nodes, and not the mesh-gradient shader, which is a soft field with no edges. A capture at 1280 px shows the mesh across the whole frame at the 48 px default, every face a triangle of visibly different shape and size, a dot at every node, about three to five accent marks at the 1 percent default in a 1280 by 800 frame, spread across it with none clustered at one edge and none under the headline or its copy, and a headline set over it readable. A capture at 390 px shows the same node spacing, so the same triangle size, with the mesh reaching the frame's edge on all four sides and no node or edge clipped into a stub. It is wrong if any quad shows both diagonals, if any two edges cross, or if a triangle is flipped; if a node dot is missing from the end of an edge; if the same seed lays out differently between mounts, between host sizes for the nodes both share, or between the two shapes; if it can be mistaken for cell-mosaic, which means any face has more than three sides; if at the minimum jitter it reads as a regular grid; or if the accent marks dominate the frame, since they are a few vertices and not a second pattern. Set meta.wraps to "content", meta.facets to ["static", "background"], meta.palette to ["fg", "accent"], and meta.demo children to a short heading over a line of copy. No meta.host, stage, controlled, or interactions. Patterns have 6144 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 3.2 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes every random number from the seed, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: cell (24 to 96 px between lattice nodes, default 48), jitter (0.1 to 0.6, the node offset as a fraction of the cell, default 0.35), nodes (boolean, draws a dot at every node, default true), marks (0 to 12, the percent of nodes drawn as accent marks, default 1), strength (0 to 1, the edges' opacity, default 0.3), seed (any integer, default 1). The inspector exposes every prop.

components.title: Step Diagonals
components.brief: Diagonals made only of square stair steps, the way a diagonal is drawn on a pixel grid. A family of parallel staircases crosses the host, and every segment of every staircase is strictly horizontal or strictly vertical: a tread of `run` times `step` px going across, then a riser of `step` px going up, repeated, with square corners. The diagonal is an effect of the repetition and no oblique segment is ever drawn, so the slope is the ratio of riser to tread: `run` 1 gives equal treads and risers, a classic 45 degree stair, and 2 or more gives a shallower one. Neighbouring staircases are `spacing` risers apart vertically, so the open channel between two of them is itself a staircase. `direction` "rising" climbs to the right and "falling" mirrors it. Draw one inline SVG on an under layer from lib/host.ts, filled with one svg pattern tile of `run` times `step` times `spacing` px wide by `step` times `spacing` px tall, overdrawn by a stroke width at its edges so corners are complete across tile seams. That is the smallest rectangle that repeats exactly: a staircase is unchanged by a shift of one tread right and one riser up, and not by a shift of one tread alone, so a tile only `run` times `step` wide would break the stair where it repeats. Strokes are one pixel in fg through cssVar, with miter joins, square caps, and crisp edges, positioned on half pixels so every line lands on one pixel row or column and never blurs across two; `step` is an integer number of pixels for the same reason. `strength` is the layer's opacity. It is a background: pointer-events none, aria-hidden, children above. Nothing moves. Follow registry/patterns/diagonal-stripes for the shape of a one family pattern with a few numeric props and the lifecycle, and registry/patterns/truchet-tiles for the inline SVG on an under layer. The nearest siblings are diagonal-stripes and the diagonals tile of truchet-tiles, and the distinction is exact. Diagonal-stripes draws straight oblique rules at any angle, with an angle prop and smooth slanted edges. Truchet diagonals draw one corner to corner oblique stroke per cell in a seeded zigzag. Step-diagonals has no angle prop, never draws an oblique stroke, and has hard square corners at a visible step size, so it reads as pixel art or a stepped ziggurat edge, which is the grid-as-medium idea in STYLE.md applied to a background. It is also not grid-paper, which draws every grid line, and not brick-lattice, which draws closed rectangles. A capture at 1280 px shows staircases of the 12 px default across the whole frame at about 45 degrees, treads and risers clearly equal, corners square, the channels between staircases four steps apart, and a headline set over it readable. A capture at 390 px shows the same step size, with the staircases cut at the frame's edge without a partial corner or stray stub, and nothing scaled down to fit. It is wrong if any segment is oblique, because then it is diagonal-stripes; if at `run` 1 a tread and a riser differ in length; if a corner is rounded or beveled, or a line is blurred across two pixel rows; if a seam shows where one pattern tile meets the next, as a gap or a doubled corner; if the step at the minimum is so small that the staircase reads as an aliased straight line instead of steps, which is why the minimum is 8 px; or if the default is loud enough that a headline set over it loses contrast on either ground. Set meta.wraps to "content", meta.facets to ["static", "background"], meta.palette to ["fg"], and meta.demo children to a short heading over a line of copy. No meta.host, stage, controlled, or interactions. Patterns have 6144 bytes, shared runtime included, and this one is expected near 1.8 KB. It fetches nothing, adds no dependency, takes no random number at all, and looks finished and intentional on both grounds.
components.props: step (8 to 40 px, the riser height and the unit of every length, default 12), run (1 to 4 treads per riser, default 1), spacing (2 to 8 risers between neighbouring staircases, default 4), direction ("rising" or "falling", default "rising"), strength (0 to 1, the layer's opacity, default 0.3). The inspector exposes every prop.
